title: Mind the Gap: Pitfalls of LLM Alignment with Asian Public Opinion
measurement_description: The paper measures the representativeness of LLMs' internal probability distributions against ground-truth public opinion on religious topics across multiple Asian nations (using Pew Research survey data). It also evaluates the models' bias, stereotyping, cultural sensitivity, and representational harms toward specific religious minority and majority groups using multiple cross-cultural benchmarks.
findings: The LLMs generally aligned well with human public opinion on broad social and political issues but consistently failed to accurately represent religious viewpoints, particularly those of minority groups. The models frequently amplified negative stereotypes and judged negative framings of specific religious identities (e.g., Shia and Sunni Muslims) as more plausible. While native-language prompting and demographic priming partially mitigated these biases and improved alignment scores, they did not entirely eliminate the underlying cultural gaps rooted in the models' predominantly Western-centric training data.
